acquisition_method.evidence: experiment types: Bottom-up proteomics; Data-dependent acquisition

alkylation_concentration.evidence: Briefly, solutions with 50 µg protein each were treated with 20 mM DTT and 40 mM acrylamide in 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate for reduction and alkylation of cysteines.

alkylation_reagent.evidence: Briefly, solutions with 50 µg protein each were treated with 20 mM DTT and 40 mM acrylamide in 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate for reduction and alkylation of cysteines.

cleavage_agent.evidence: Beads with bound proteins were washed with 80% ethanol (three times) and subjected to tryptic digestion at 37 °C, 18 h using a trypsin-protein ratio of 1:25.

collision_energy.evidence: Ions with z>1 were subjected to higher-energy collision induced dissociation (HCD: 1.0 Da quadrupole isolation, threshold intensity 25,000, collision energy 27%) and fragments analyzed in the Orbitrap (R=15,000).

fragmentation_method.evidence: Ions with z>1 were subjected to higher-energy collision induced dissociation (HCD: 1.0 Da quadrupole isolation, threshold intensity 25,000, collision energy 27%) and fragments analyzed in the Orbitrap (R=15,000).

mass_analyzer.evidence: inferred: Ions between 330 and 1600 m/z were scanned in the Orbitrap every 3 seconds (R=120,000).

ptm.evidence: Tryptic peptides (Trypsin/P) with up to two missed cleavages were searched, propionamide was set as a static modification of cysteines, while oxidation of methionine and isotope label on lysine (+8) were set as dynamic modifications.
